messages:
Leah: Hey team :wave: quick heads-up — planning an RBAC cleanup + log-export sampling change next week. Need input on vuln triage retention and KMS rotation impact.

Raj: tl;dr what are we changing exactly?

Leah: Two parts: 1) Reduce noisy debug-level export retention from 90d -> 30d for cost. 2) Create a small persistent retention bucket (365d) for auth/privilege escalation signals we keep for vuln investigations.

Mia: OK on the retention windows. Who owns the 365d set? We should limit access strictly.

Leah: Proposal: map the 365d exports to a new service account `sec-vuln-archive-sa` with read-only role. Access via ticketing + 7d temporary grant with MFA enforced.

Jordan: How does KMS factor in? Do we rotate export keys? Any downstream consumers will break if we rewrap without coordination.

Leah: Good call. Plan is to rotate the CMK and rewrap existing export bundles. We will keep a transitional key alias for 30d for backward compatibility, then retire. Need to validate unwrap/rewrap script.

Sam: Can you share the rewrap snippet? I can run a dry-run in staging.

Leah: sample aws CLI for rewrap (staging):
```bash
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/sec-archive-new --plaintext fileb://export.bin --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > export.rewrapped.bin
```
This is simplified — real pipeline will stream and sign.

Raj: A couple of risks: 1) Export consumers that expect old key alias. 2) Search/alert indices might re-ingest differently if we change compression. Add schema checks.

Mia: Also: vuln triage team wants full request headers for 180d for deep investigations. That conflicts with our cost policy. Can we sample auth failures at 100% for 365d but keep success auth events sampled 1%?

Leah: Yes — propose sampling config: auth_failures: 100%, auth_success: 1%, debug:* : 0.1% (or 1 in 1000). We'll document in the SIEM ingest pipeline config.

Jordan: How do we implement sampling without changing producers? Can we do it at the SIEM-ingest lambda?

Sam: We can. Add a sampling stage post-collector that tags and forwards to different retention sinks. Performance impact should be minimal if we batch. I'll bench in staging.

Mia: We must also update RBAC: remove `logs:exporter` from dev role, add `logs:exporter` to `sec-vuln-archive-sa` and `forensics-oncall` role. Any objections?

Raj: I want a short embargo window before we remove dev access — say 48h notice, export logs of current consumer usage to make sure nobody breaks.

Leah: Agreed. Plan timeline:
- Day 0: Announce (this thread)
- Day 2: Freeze changes, collect consumer list via telemetry
- Day 4: Apply RBAC changes in staging + sampling config
- Day 7: KMS rotate in staging + rewrap dry-run
- Day 10: Prod rollout (canary 10% then full)

Sam: I'll own staging bench and perf numbers.

Jordan: I'll coordinate KMS rotate with infra and maintain alias for 30d.

Mia: I'll update the ticketing template for temporary access and add required justification fields.

Raj: I'll prepare rollback playbook and an alert to detect missing export consumers.

deploy-bot: export-job-scheduler — canary export job scheduled for 2025-05-08T03:00Z (job id ej-1122) :white_check_mark:

Leah: Thanks all. If no major blockers, I'll open the RFC doc and PR for the RBAC changes today. Please add comments in the RFC. :thumbsup:
